title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Hessian Approximation: A Single-Step Policy Optimization Lens (ZoVH)

claims.summary: Prop 3.2/3.3: the (u u^T - I) form (any baseline) and rank-one form (baseline F_mu) coincide exactly (||diff||=0 with b=F_mu) and both -> grad^2 F_mu.

Theorem 4.6: E[Ĥ]=grad^2 F_mu, BASELINE-INDEPENDENT. Verified by (a) Ĥ(b1)-Ĥ(b2)->0 at 1/sqrt(N) (tracks ||mean(u u^T-I)||), (b) mean(Ĥ)-> analytic smoothed Hessian (quadratic A; quartic diag(12 theta^2+12 mu^2)).

Theorem 4.7/4.8: optimal baseline b*->F_mu as d grows (||u u^T-I||_F^2 concentrates); variance term decreases ~1/K; squared smoothing bias ||grad^2 F_mu-grad^2 f||_F^2 ~ 12 mu^2 sqrt(d), bounded by L2^2 mu^2 d.

Figure 2 (ZoVH vs central-difference): the bare estimator's 1/mu^4 variance dominates central-difference truncation error, so ZoVH does NOT beat central-diff at equal query budget. The paper's 8x improvement requires its full control-variate / query-reuse machinery, not in the bare Prop 3.2 estimator.
MNIST adversarial attack - real data, deferred.

Section 6.2 (22x ZO speedup): ZO gradient noise (~mu^2 d/iter) and Hessian-estimate noise prevent the bare ZoVH-preconditioned step from out-converging vanilla ZO-GD; the 22x speedup needs the paper's full variance-reduced implementation.

honest_notes: This paper came in at 6 pts (below the >=10 target) because claims C4/C6 are empirical speedups that do not reproduce with the bare ZoVH estimator -- the paper's headline accuracy/speedup gains rely on its full variance-reduction machinery (control variates, specific query-reuse protocol) which is not captured by the closed-form Prop 3.2 estimator.

The 3 verified claims (C1/C2/C3) are rigorous and machine-precision-derivable: the unbiasedness E[Ĥ]=grad^2 F_mu (baseline-independent, converges to the analytic smoothed Hessian) and the bias-variance decomposition are exact.
Per the challenge honesty bar, C4/C6 are reported as honest negatives rather than force-fit.
